texts.arguments: 3. Ms. Shalaka Srivastava, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the learned trial Court and appellate court have erred in law as well as on facts in passing the impugned judgment. She further submits that all the prosecution witnesses have made contradictory statements and from the materials brought on record, it is apparent that the prosecution has failed to prove the charge leveled against the petitioner and as per the record, no case is made out against the petitioner. She further submits that the court below failed to consider that the District Board is not a local authority nor does the district medical officer has any right to sanction. The analysis was never Mahadeo Dutta vs The State Of Jharkhand. ..... Opposite ... on 23 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3977428/ 1 communicated to the petitioner and as a result he was prevented to send the same for the analysis in accordance with law and the same has never been communicated to the accused persons. She further contended that the appellate Court has not considered the fact that as per PW, the shop of the petitioner is in an open space, and also when the inspection and seizure list was being prepared there was heavy rain and dust which could have affected the quality of black pepper and also it was ceased in wet condition. The pepper was ceased, the panelist had given a report that it was substandard and no adulteration was recorded. However, substandard and adulteration are two different things. She reiterated that no allegation was established, whatsoever, of adulteration of black pepper by the learned trial and appellate court and the complaint itself is not maintainable under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. She lastly submits that the sample of the seized articles was not taken in accordance with the law. Alternatively, she submits that the instant case is of the year 1976 and about 46 years have elapsed and now the petitioner is about 66 years and he must have suffered mental agony for ongoing litigation and at present. She further submits that the petitioner has never misused the privilege of bail and he is not a habitual offender, as such some leniency may be granted by this Court. 4. Learned A.P.P. opposes the contention of the petitioner and submits that there is concurrent finding and as such, no interference is required. 5.
